0.long_answer: Congenital mesoblastic nephroma is the most common kidney neoplasm diagnosed in the first three months of life. Studies have demonstrated that many of these tumors harbor the ETV6-NTRK3 fusion gene, which arises from a translocation t(12;15)(p13;q25). This event fuses the ETV6 gene on chromosome 12 with the NTRK3 gene on chromosome 15, creating a chimeric protein with constitutive tyrosine kinase activity that drives tumor growth.
